drug_class: Beta-blocker (non-selective beta-adrenergic blocker with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity)
purpose: Pindolol is mainly used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Keeping your blood pressure under control helps lower your risk of having a heart attack, stroke, or kidney problems. Your doctor may also use it for other heart-related conditions.
how_it_works: Your heart has special receptors that respond to adrenaline, which can make your heart beat faster and harder. Pindolol blocks those receptors, so your heart beats more slowly and with less force, which lowers your blood pressure. Unlike some other beta-blockers, pindolol also has a mild stimulating effect on the heart, which means it is less likely to slow your heart rate too much.
common_side_effects: You might feel tired or dizzy, especially when you first start taking it. Some people notice cold hands and feet, trouble sleeping, or mild stomach upset like nausea. Dizziness when standing up quickly can also happen.
warnings: Do not stop taking pindolol suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, diabetes, or any breathing problems, because pindolol can make these conditions worse or hide signs of low blood sugar. Also let your doctor know all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with pindolol.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to a maximum of 60 mg per day depending on how your body responds. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you to.
